Use 16 bit indexes in curve renderer when possible

Using 32 bit indexes breaks batching, so this can have a large
impact on scenes with a lot of shapes.

This also requires that we set RequiresFullMatrix to disable batching
on gradient and texture fills. This was a pre-existing bugs for these
modes, but since we used 32-bit indexes, batching was implicitly
disabled anyway, so it wasn't noticed.

Note: This expands the RequiresDeterminant requirement of the curve
fill material to RequiresFullMatrixExceptTranslate. Merging rotated
fills does not work correctly because of the antialiasing. In practice
it makes no difference currently, because RequiresDeterminant does
exactly the same as RequiresFullMatrixExceptTranslate, but if we ever
enable this distinction in the future, the flags should be set
correctly.

a11y: Send value change events for items given a role from QML

QQuickAccessibleAttached connects the value and cursorPosition change
signals of its item in the constructor, for the interfaces the role of
the item provides. An item that gets its role from Accessible.role has
no role yet at that time, so an Item with Accessible.role:
Accessible.Slider and a value property never told assistive technology
about a new value.

Connect the signals again when the role changes. Controls were not
affected, their role comes from accessibleRole() and is known when the
attached object is created.

controls, also when accessibility becomes active after the item exists,
as on wasm where the user enables the screen reader support.

Menu: Sync with requested popup type in makeEditMenu()

QQuickContextMenu calls makeEditMenu() for text-editing controls once
the menu resolves to Popup.Native, but before the menu is shown. The
native handle is only created on component completion, or when the
menu becomes visible, so if popupType was switched to Popup.Native
after the menu was created, e.g. from ContextMenu.onRequested, we
would dereference a null handle:

    frame #0: QtQuickTemplates2`QQuickMenuPrivate::makeEditMenu(this=0x00000076f8f83300) at qquickmenu.cpp:594:13
    frame #1: QtQuickTemplates2`QQuickContextMenu::event(this=0x00000076f8d49880, event=0x000000016fdfae08) at qquickcontextmenu.cpp:253:43
    frame #2: QtQuick`QQuickItemPrivate::handleContextMenuEvent(this=0x00000076fb3f6c00, event=0x000000016fdfae08) at qquickitem.cpp:5907:36

We now sync with the requested popup type if we don't have a handle
yet, which creates it. The sync is skipped while the menu is visible,
as switching between native and non-native only takes effect on the
next open, so we still guard against a missing handle.

QtQmlModels: Fix crash in ListModel::sync() when a move is a no-op

ListModel::sync() emits move notifications to transform the old target
row order into the new source order. For each element it calls
beginMoveRows(parent, targetIndex, targetIndex, parent, i) followed
unconditionally by endMoveRows().

beginMoveRows() returns false and does NOT push onto the model's
internal change stack when the move is a no-op (destination i equal to
targetIndex or targetIndex + 1). The subsequent endMoveRows() then pops
an empty stack and dereferences out-of-bounds memory, which is only
caught by Q_ASSERT(validMove) in debug builds. In release builds this is
undefined behaviour and crashes with a SIGSEGV inside
QAbstractItemModelPrivate::movePersistentIndexes().

This is reproducible from a WorkerScript that syncs a filtered ListModel
while the main thread also removes rows (QTBUG-63976 / QTBUG-63935): the
sync bookkeeping can compute a no-op move.

Only call endMoveRows() and run the index fixup for an accepted move.
The target element vector is rebuilt in the correct order earlier in
sync(), so skipping the no-op notification keeps the data consistent and
just avoids emitting a redundant (and invalid) move.

QSG render loops: Recreate the swapchain when it is out of date

When beginFrame() or endFrame() reported FrameOpSwapChainOutOfDate,
both the threaded and the basic render loop kept the same swapchain
unless the window size had changed. The size often stays the same:
NVIDIA's Vulkan driver, for one, reports VK_ERROR_OUT_OF_DATE_KHR when
the Wayland compositor updates the surface's dmabuf feedback. Every
following frame then failed the same way and the window never rendered
again (on Wayland it also ended up unexposed, as the frame callback
requested for the failed frame never arrived). Vulkan requires
recreating the swapchain in this case.

Remember that the swapchain is out of date and recreate it before the
next frame, as for a size change. The basic render loop now also
schedules that next frame instead of waiting for an unrelated update.

Quick tests: Use the MouseCursorPositioning capability

qtbase commit 1e275f5ea5ec2227f078f12c3dc004a7383af527
("Add QPlatformIntegration::MouseCursorPositioning capability") added
a QPA capability telling whether the platform supports programmatic
cursor positioning via QCursor::setPos(), and changed the qtbase auto
tests that rely on it to check the capability instead of hard-coded
platform names or runtime checks of the cursor position.

QuickTestUtils calls QCursor::setPos() in QQuickTest::initView() and
the moveMouseAway() helpers only to get the cursor out of the way,
and already skips this on Wayland. On other platforms without cursor
positioning, such as OHOS, QPlatformCursor::setPos() emits a "This
plugin does not support QCursor::setPos()" warning instead. Tests
using the FailOnWarnings policy then fail in the first test function
that shows a view, even if they do not depend on the cursor position,
e.g. tst_QQmlTreeModel::appendToEmptyModel(). Since moving the cursor
away is only a best-effort precaution, skip it, rather than the test,
when the capability is not available.

Also check the capability in the tests that need the system cursor
to actually move, instead of checking for Wayland or Android, or
probing whether QCursor::setPos() works at runtime. Without the
capability, QCursor::setPos() at best emulates a mouse move within
the application; this cannot move the cursor outside a window, and
QCursor::pos() may still report the old position. So only the tests
that move the cursor outside the window, or that verify a result
based on QCursor::pos(), are changed. Tests that only need the
emulated mouse move inside the window are left as they are, so that
they keep running on platforms without the capability.

QQuickItem: don't complete a layer created during componentComplete

QQuickItem::componentComplete() sets componentComplete before updating
the anchors. If anything reads the layer property during that update
(such as an onWidthChanged handler, or qt.quick.viewport logging via
QQmlContext::nameForObject()), QQuickItemPrivate::layer() creates a
layer that is already complete. componentComplete() then completed it
again, which hit the Q_ASSERT in QQuickItemLayer::componentComplete()
in debug builds and, for an enabled layer, created a second effect
source in release builds.

Complete only the layer that existed before componentComplete was set.

Amends a6eb09137247a880c58995464a35c1ad5c3f0c20 ("Fixed some
Item.layer bugs and added auto-tests."), which added the Q_ASSERTs and
made QQuickItemPrivate::layer() create an already-complete layer once
componentComplete is set. The order of the steps in componentComplete()
dates from 42d6acd0a3ea5fa5cf7ab69f1f8f2206559107ea ("Introduce
layerering support (ShaderEffectSource) directly in Item"), where
completing a layer twice was harmless.

3d3de0f5a47a249a0229edcca18cf71826bd4bc0 ("Include QML object id in
QQuickItem debug output") didn't cause the bug, but made
qt.quick.viewport logging trigger it: printing a child item calls
nameForObject(), which reads the layer property of the child's context
object. This is the crash reported in QTBUG-142250.

Add public API to create a QML preview target for executables

An executable target might not be using qt_add_qml_module itself, but
only launch QML from library targets. We currently don't have a
convenient way to preview such a target. Add qt6_add_qml_preview as an
explicit opt in.

Unless QT_QML_NO_QML_PREVIEW is set, all executable targets will get a
preview target if they (transitively) link against Qt6::Qml. Individual
targets can still opt out by setting the QT_QML_NO_QML_PREVIEW target
property. If the global behavior is turned off, qt6_add_qml_preview can
be used to enable it for a given target.

get a module_qmlpreview target by default. This can be changed by
setting QT_QML_NO_QML_PREVIEW.

Pick a large enough pooled vertex/index buffer when there is one

When unmap() takes a buffer from the pool, a buffer that fits was
never preferred over an already picked one that is too small. So if
the first buffer in the pool was too small, it won even when a large
enough one was available, and then got resized, meaning the native
buffer was recreated.

Recreating buffers is particularly expensive with OpenGL on NVIDIA,
where generating a new buffer name waits for the driver's worker
thread. In a scripted Qt Quick Controls application shell (lists,
editors, animated shapes; from sgbench) with OpenGL on Windows,
the render thread CPU time per frame goes from 0.89 ms to 0.45 ms
(-50%), the whole process from 1.53 ms to 1.09 ms (-29%).

Hide items by blocking their node instead of using opacity 0

...in order to avoid frequent rebuilds of the batch renderer data
structures. This patch is a different approach to the core idea in
change 511418.

Hidden items (either explicit or due to layer/ShaderEffectSource) were
kept out of the rendered scene by inserting a QSGOpacityNode with
opacity 0.

Since a4fb90f223 (QTBUG-85965), the batch renderer does a full rebuild
of all batches whenever a subtree gets blocked or unblocked together
with an opacity change, so every hide and show re-processed and
re-uploaded the whole scene. Views culling delegates and controls
culling their content do this frequently, so generally this is not great
for performance and CPU load.

Instead, do it differently: set a new internal QSGNode::IsNodeBlocked
flag on the item's transform node, derived from explicitVisible and
hideRefCount, and mark it DirtySubtreeBlocked when it changes. The
software renderer never checked isSubtreeBlocked(), so it now treats a
blocked transform node like opacity 0. As a drive-by fix, as hiding no
longer goes through the opacity node, an OpacityAnimator running on a
culled or hidden item no longer makes it visible (which was an unrelated
bug).

This in itself makes the full-rebuild-if-blocked-subtree-has-an-
opacity-change addition in a4fb90f223 disfunctional. That is however not
an issue, because that full rebuild worked around batches being drawn in
the wrong order after a batch's first element was removed. That needed
an element to join a batch across an overlapping element of another
batch, which 9aa3db2e19 (Don't invalidate unaffected render orders)
ruled out for the default batching in 2021.

The full-rebuild workaround is therefore only kept in the unlikely case
of building with QSGBATCHRENDERER_INVALIDATE_WEDGED_NODES defined. That
restores the old batching, and so then we will keep hiding items like
before, to ensure everything continues to works correctly.

The manual test tests/manual/hiddenitems hides and shows 40 items in a
clipped panel every frame, in front of a static scene of 3000 cells, and
reports sync and render CPU time per frame. On D3D11, culling,
hideSource, visible and opacity toggles go from about 1030 us per frame
with a full rebuild in every frame to about 270 us with partial
rebuilds.

Note that this does not solve the issue of full rebuilds when showing
again content that is not clipped, or does not have a batch root above
for some other reason.

However, when hiding, the fix helps avoiding full rebuilds in any case.

QtQml: Fix enum key shadowing

The first time we perform an enum lookup on a type, we call initEnums to
ensure we collect and cache all available enums and their keys. There,
we call insertEnumsFromPropertyCache which inserts enums found on meta
objects for the type and then also walks the property cache hierarchy to
collect enums on base QML types.

This works fine except when performing unqualified lookups. In that
case, the lookup by key name is done on a single QStringHash holding a
mapping from all keys to their value.

The problem is in how that Hash is populated. Firstly, Cpp types are
walked after QML types. And, secondly, QML types are walked from most
derived to least derived. This way, each time an enum key is found, it
is added to the hash and potentially overrides the values found
previously in shadowing enums. This can lead to the wrong value being
returned when performing unqualified lookups to shadowing keys.

To fix this, walk Cpp types before QML types, and walk QML types in
deriving order.

The reproducer in the linked issue performed lookups to entries such as
TopLeft on a type having access to two enums providing those keys in its
hierarchy: QQuickItem::TransformOrigin and Selectionhandle::Position.

  enum TransformOrigin {
      TopLeft,    Top,    TopRight,
      Left,       Center, Right,
      BottomLeft, Bottom, BottomRight
  };

  enum Position {
      TopLeft,    Top,    TopRight,
      Left,               Right,
      BottomLeft, Bottom, BottomRight,
      NPositions
  }

Only the keys pointing to edges were ever queried. Since Position does
not contain a Center key, the keys starting from Right have different
values on the two enums.

Because of the lookup issue described above, the wrong values were
returned for those keys. This still doesn't cause any issues in most
cases as the descrepancy happens identically in all places performing
the lookup.

Because the issue does not affect AOT compiled bindings, only when an
enum lookup is performed in two bindings expecting the same value but
being compiled differently do problems appear on the reproducer. These
cause a mismatch in which handle was considered selected, leading to an
assert in debug and incorrect handle behavior in release..

tst_QQuickPointHandler: Fix tabletStylus() at fractional DPR

tabletStylus() computed the expected translation() by converting the
10-pixel native delta with QHighDpi::fromNativeLocalPosition() on a
QPoint, which rounds to the nearest local pixel. translation() is a
QVector2D built from an unrounded QPointF subtraction
(position() - pressPosition()), so it carries whatever fractional
remainder the conversion produces.

At an integer devicePixelRatio the rounding step is a no-op, so the
rounded expectation happened to match the unrounded result. At a
fractional devicePixelRatio (for instance, in HarmonyOS - 1.9), the
two diverge: 10 native pixels divided by 1.9 rounds to 5 local pixels,
while the handler's unrounded translation is 5.263 (with fractional
part) failing the QCOMPARE.

Compare translation() against a QPointF-based, unrounded conversion
of the delta instead, so the comparison uses the same precision as
the value under test.

Fix crash when recycling batch root text nodes

When we recycle glyph nodes, we reset properties that have
been set by the renderer as it visited the nodes originally
because we don't want information leaking from earlier runs
into the update. One such propert is the renderer matrix.

We therefore implicitly depend on the batch renderer's
Updater to revisit the nodes to set the correct values
again once they have been updated.

For the normal case, this would work as follows: The text
node calls updatePaintNode(), which dirties the matrix
and this triggers an update pass over all children which
updates the required properties since the text node and
its children are in the coordinate space of their batch
root.

In the case where the text node itself is a batch root,
however, the children are in its coordinate space. So
dirtying just its matrix does not trigger an update of
children. This leaves a null pointer for its matrix and
causes a crash later. The threshold for making the text
node a batch root is 64 children by default, so the added
test checks this.

The fix is to force an update pass on the children when we
know that we have recycled glyphs in the tree.

Fix stale pointers in multitexture distance field cache

When the distance field cache grew, we would sometimes keep pointers
around to stale data. This latent bug was likely not caught in Qt 5
days because of QList reallocation behavior. In Qt 6, it became easier
to reproduce due to the use of QVector instead.

It also required displaying enough unique glyphs on a device with a
low enough maximum texture size to trigger, which is likely why it has
not been encountered before now.

There were two possible cases of stale pointers: One was that we
stored pointers to the TextureInfos in QSGRhiDistanceFieldGlyphCache and
later appended new textures to the list, making all the stored pointers
stale.

In addition, the pointer to the Texture data in QSGDistanceFieldCache
was shared with the material reading it. If the material was active when
the m_textures array was resized, those pointers would also go stale. We
fix this by allocating each Texture entry individually instead and
deleting them when the cache is deleted.

This also adds an environment variable that can be used to override the
system max texture size for testing purposes.

CMake: Avoid duplicated qml type registration commands in VS and make

Visual Studio and Makefile generators copy a custom command into every
target that needs one of the command outputs, unless the target
depends on another target that already owns the command.

${target}_qmltyperegistration depends on the generated
qmltyperegistrations.cpp file, and transitively on the outputs of
moc --collect-json, the automoc json file list extraction and, when
CMake depfiles are used (CMake 4.4+ for Visual Studio), the
cmake_autogen timestamp. It doesn't depend on the module target or on
${target}_autogen, so all of these commands end up in both the
module target and ${target}_qmltyperegistration.

The two targets don't depend on each other, so the copies can run in
parallel.
This happens e.g. when building the whole solution in Visual Studio,
or with a Makefile generator when a target depends on both the module
target and one of its qmllint targets.
The commands then race on writing the same files, which fails with
errors like
  moc: Cannot create .../moc_Object.cpp. Error: Permission denied

Setting QT_USE_CMAKE_DEPFILES to OFF only gets rid of the duplicated
cmake_autogen command. The duplicated moc --collect-json and
qmltyperegistrar commands are present regardless of that option.

To fix these issues, make ${target}_qmltyperegistration depend on the
module target for Visual Studio and Makefile generators, like we
already do for Xcode. The generators then don't copy the commands
anymore.
The consequence is that the qmllint targets build the module target
first with these generators as well.

Making the module target depend on ${target}_qmltyperegistration
instead is not possible, because that creates a dependency cycle with
the ${target}_autogen_timestamp_deps target that CMake creates.

It might be possible to avoid that by setting AUTOGEN_ORIGIN_DEPENDS
to OFF, but then we'd have to re-create a lot of dependencies, and
it's unclear if that is in the end viable.

Ninja is not affected, because it has a single build edge per output.

An "import Foo auto" in a qmldir inherits the version the module itself
was imported in. The engine uses the version the import has resolved
to, though, not the requested one. If you import a module without a
version, or with only a major version, its dependencies are therefore
imported with the latest version of the module, not without version.

version-decorated subdirectories for such qmldir-imported modules.
Since we don't search version-decorated directories for direct
unversioned imports, we shouldn't do that for their dependencies either.

Make this consistent by:
1, passing the resolved version on to "auto" imports in QQmlJSImporter.
2, searching for "auto" imports only in the version-decorated

   QQmlTypeLoader and in QQmlJSImporter.
3, Honoring the new "export" entry in qmldir in both QQmlJSImporter and
   the engine. The versions explicitly exported are always available,
   no matter what components are declared.

This is actually a potential miscompilation as the qmlcppcodegen test
shows. Therefore we have to pick it back.

Since we now actually detect when a module is imported using a version
it doesn't support, a few qmllint tests have to be adapted. We either
add a supported version where that was intended or change the error
message where the test was intended to fail.

Don't let distance field glyphs cross texture boundaries

The glyph cache uses a single area allocator spanning all its
textures stacked vertically, each the size of the maximum texture
size. Since the allocator had no knowledge of the texture
boundaries, a glyph could be allocated across the boundary between
two textures. It would then be assigned to the upper texture, which
would grow beyond the maximum texture size, causing texture creation
to fail.

This adds an optional slice height to QSGAreaAllocator. When set, a
free node which spans a slice boundary is split at the boundary
before allocating, so that allocations always end up within a
single slice. The glyph cache uses the maximum texture size as slice
height, so glyphs which do not fit at the bottom of one texture are
moved to the next one.

animating towards 0), the minimal inner radius could cover the whole
gradient length. Gradient stops counted in vertexCount were then never
reached and never inserted, which triggered
Q_ASSERT(index == vertexCount).

Insert all remaining gradient stops before the last vertex, and keep
the inserted vertices and their interpolation within the current
segment.

The documentation for requesting an animation frame on a Canvas is a
single sentence. It doesn't say why you would use it, that the callback
runs only once, what argument it receives, or that it runs only while
the canvas is visible. It also doesn't say where drawing should happen.

draw in the paint handler and wonder why it stays silent while an
animation runs.

in the callback is shown in that same frame without asking for a
repaint. Add a short animated example and a link to the cancel
counterpart. Readers get a working pattern to copy instead of
reverse-engineering the behavior.

QQmlTypeData: Ignore stale errors from loadDependentImports

When we call loadDependentImports from loadImplicitImport, it might put
errors into the error list, even though importing doesn't fail (e.g.
from failing to load a plugin from a module in qrc, but later picking
the plugin up from the actual file system).
This happens because QQmlTypeLoader::locateLocalQmldir might populate
errors, but might still succeed later.

So don't rely on the error list being empty as the indicator of whether
there was an issue, but instead explicitly track it.

In a future commit, we might want to ensure that locateLocalQmldir
doesn't actually stores irrelevant errors, but this more minimal fix is
more suitable for older branches.

qmlcachegen: Read response files as UTF-8

The response file that CMake generates for qmlcachegen's loader
generation is always UTF-8 encoded, because CMake handles strings as
UTF-8 internally on all platforms. qmlcachegen decoded it with
QString::fromLocal8Bit(), which on Windows uses the ANSI code page.
With a non-ASCII resource path such as "Bäh.qml", the loader then got
a different mangled name than the compilation unit, whose path is
passed on the command line. The link failed with undefined symbols,
and the runtime lookup key was wrong as well.

This showed up when building tst_qmlcachegen on a Windows host for a
UNIX target.

Decode the response file as UTF-8 instead, so that qmlcachegen
generates the same identifiers on every host platform.

Quick examples: use Qt Quick Controls for the example launcher

The Qt Quick examples presented their sub-demos with a bespoke
LauncherList/SimpleLauncherDelegate from examples/quick/shared.
Referencing code outside an example's own directory violates QUIP-13 and
prevents copying an example out of the example tree.

Replace that launcher with one built from Qt Quick Controls: each
example's entry QML is now an ApplicationWindow with a StackView and a
ToolBar back button, loaded via QQmlApplicationEngine. The StackView's
initial item is a ListView of ItemDelegates driven by a plain JS array.
Each example has its own copy of LauncherList.qml and
SimpleLauncherDelegate.qml, so it no longer depends on files outside its
directory.

Sub-demos are pushed wrapped in a Loader, which is a focus scope like in
the old launcher. Without it, StackView gives focus to the sub-demo's
root item, and items inside it that set focus: true, such as the
GridView in views, do not get keyboard input.

Converted: animation, canvas, draganddrop, imageelements,
particles/{affectors,emitters,imageparticle,system}, positioners,
quickshapes/shapes, text and views. The corresponding now-unused
reused_dir_targets entries are removed.

pointerhandlers deliberately does not use Qt Quick Controls: it
demonstrates building components from scratch with pointer handlers, so
it keeps the old launcher. It gets its own copy of the launcher files,
which makes it self-contained and runnable directly with
"qml pointerhandlers.qml".

quickshapes/shapes still uses the shared module for the Images singleton
referenced by one of its sub-demos.
